findings.title: change_password drops session-secret rotation, breaking the codebase's own established convention for this exact problem
findings.problem: Global CLAUDE.md: 'Everything else — style, structure, architecture — yields to the existing codebase's conventions: before introducing a new pattern, check how the same problem is solved elsewhere in the repo and follow that.' This diff deletes session_secret rotation + cookie re-issuance from change_password, while the same file's reset_confirm (lines ~1937-2011) still implements the identical pattern for the identical problem (invalidate all other sessions when the credential changes), with extensive 'D-12' design comments explaining why. STATE.md explicitly documents this as a shared convention: 'Track A's reset-confirm session rotation reuses the v2.8.1 change_password rotation pattern.' The diff breaks that consistency instead of following it.
findings.fix_hint: Restore new_session_secret = generate_session_secret(), include session_secret in the model_copy update, and re-issue the acting user's cookie signed with the new secret (mirror reset_confirm's D-12 block, lines 1937-2011 of the current file).
findings.why_it_matters: This silently reintroduces the exact vulnerability commit 0866332 ('fix(auth): rotate session secret on password change to evict other sessions') deliberately fixed and SECURITY.md documents as a control ('Session-secret rotation on password change (CWE-613) ... prevents credential-change bypass via a stolen session token'): a stolen/compromised cookie now survives a password change for the full 30-day COOKIE_MAX_AGE. Verified by running the suite: tests/test_auth_routes.py::test_change_password_rotates_session_secret_and_persists FAILS against this diff.

members.title: Restore session revocation on password change
members.problem: Updating only password_hash preserves the existing session_secret. An attacker holding a cookie issued before the password change can still access protected routes afterward: AuthMiddleware accepts it at triggarr/web/middleware.py:146–148, and validate_session checks only its signature and age, not the password hash. That access persists until the cookie's 30-day expiry. The reset endpoint's rotation does not protect this password-change path.

members.title: Password change no longer rotates session_secret, so sessions on other devices stay valid
members.problem: The diff deletes the session_secret rotation from change_password and keeps only the password_hash update. A session cookie is signed from the username and session_secret alone (sign_session(username, secret) in triggarr/auth.py:79). It is not tied to the password hash. The middleware check in triggarr/web/middleware.py:146 uses the same unchanged secret, so every cookie issued before the change still passes. That includes a stolen or compromised cookie, which stays valid for up to COOKIE_MAX_AGE (30 days). I found no other code that does this job: the only other rotation is in the password-reset path (routes.py:1941), which this endpoint never reaches. Three existing tests fail against the working tree: test_change_password_rotates_session_secret_and_persists, test_change_password_reissues_acting_user_cookie and test_change_password_evicts_other_device_session (I ran them; 3 failed, 5 passed). Removing this protection also breaks the project's 'All tests pass' rule.
source_window: context={"errors": {"new_password": "Password must be 72 characters or fewer"}},
members.why_it_matters: A user who changes their password because a session might be compromised gets no protection: the attacker's cookie keeps working for up to 30 days.
members.fix_hint: restore generate_session_secret() rotation in the model_copy update, and re-issue the acting user's cookie signed with the new secret

members.title: change_password drops session-secret rotation while the sibling credential flow (reset confirm) keeps it, so the two credential-change paths now behave differently
members.problem: The codebase has an established rule: every credential change rotates the session secret and re-issues the acting user's cookie. Before this diff, two places followed it: change_password (the lines this diff removes) and the password-reset confirm route (routes.py ~1941-2009: generate_session_secret, an H2 read-back guard, then sign_session with COOKIE_MAX_AGE and is_secure_request). This diff removes the rule from change_password only. After it, a password reset logs out every other device but a normal password change does not. SECURITY.md line 45 still advertises rotation on password change. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-02-recovery-counts-config-design.md:57 justifies the reset flow's rotation as having the 'same rationale as `change_password`', and 2026-06-02-launch-hardening-design.md:125 lists 'session-secret rotation on password change' as shipped v2.8 hardening.
source_window: context={"errors": {"new_password": "Password must be 72 characters or fewer"}},
members.why_it_matters: Someone who changes their password because they think a session was stolen expects that session to be cut off. After this change, a stolen session keeps working after a password change, which contradicts the project's published security policy (CWE-613).
members.fix_hint: Restore the rotation and cookie re-issue in change_password, matching the reset-confirm flow. If dropping it is deliberate, update SECURITY.md, both specs and the reset flow's rationale in the same change, and make the reset/change asymmetry an explicit documented choice.

intent_doc_match.quote: Session-secret rotation on password change (CWE-613) -- when a user changes their password, a new session secret is generated and the current session is re-keyed. This invalidates all prior sessions, preventing credential-change bypass via a stolen session token.

members.title: Password change no longer rotates session_secret, so compromised/stolen sessions survive a password change
members.problem: The diff removes session_secret rotation from change_password (and the matching cookie re-issue/log line). Previously, new_auth rotated both password_hash and session_secret in one update, invalidating every cookie signed with the old secret via validate_session(cookie, auth.session_secret.get_secret_value()) (used in AuthMiddleware and login_page). Now only password_hash changes, so any existing session cookie -- including one held by an attacker who prompted the password change -- remains valid for the full 30-day COOKIE_MAX_AGE after the password is changed.
source_window: context={"errors": {"new_password": "Password must be 72 characters or fewer"}},
members.why_it_matters: The entire point of invalidating sessions on password change is to lock out an intruder who has a stolen session cookie -- the most common reason a user changes their password. Without secret rotation, an attacker with an existing valid cookie keeps full account access even after the legitimate user 'secures' the account by changing the password.
members.fix_hint: restore session_secret rotation (generate_session_secret()) alongside password_hash in the same model_copy/atomic write, and re-issue the acting request's cookie under the new secret, matching the pattern still present in reset_confirm_post (routes.py:1937-2011)

members.title: Changing the password no longer revokes existing sessions; stolen cookies stay valid for up to 30 days
members.problem: The diff removes session_secret rotation from change_password and does not add anything that does the same job. Session cookies are only checked by validate_session(cookie, auth.session_secret) (triggarr/web/middleware.py:146, triggarr/auth.py:113, max_age=COOKIE_MAX_AGE = 30 days). The signed payload is just the username. It does not depend on password_hash, so a new password hash alone invalidates nothing. Before this diff, rotating the secret was the only way to revoke sessions: _sync_auth_state (routes.py:108) only toggles UI flags, and no session store or denylist exists. Concrete path: an attacker holding a stolen triggarr_session cookie sends any authenticated request after the owner changes their password. Middleware step 4 (middleware.py:146-148) still validates it against the unchanged secret, so the attacker keeps full access, including the settings and API-key pages, for the rest of the cookie's 30-day max_age. The password reset flow (routes.py:1941-2009) still rotates the secret, so the two credential-change paths now behave differently.
source_window: context={"errors": {"new_password": "Password must be 72 characters or fewer"}},
members.why_it_matters: Changing your password is how you recover when a session may be compromised. With this diff the step does nothing against an attacker who already has a cookie, and the UI still shows 'Password updated', so the user is wrongly reassured. The removed comment in the diff states this exact intent.
members.fix_hint: Restore generate_session_secret() rotation and re-issue the acting user's cookie, matching the reset-confirm path at routes.py:1941-2009, or bind sessions to a password_hash-derived value.

findings.title: Diff breaks four existing tests that assert session rotation on password change
findings.problem: These tests assert the behavior the diff removes: tests/test_auth_routes.py:604 test_change_password_rotates_session_secret_and_persists, :641 test_change_password_reissues_acting_user_cookie, :677 test_change_password_evicts_other_device_session, and tests/test_auth_integration.py:182 test_password_change_invalidates_old_sessions. With the rotation and cookie re-issue gone, they should fail. CLAUDE.md requires `pytest tests/ -x` to pass before pushing, so this diff cannot ship cleanly unless the tests are deleted, which would remove the only regression guard on this control.
findings.fix_hint: Revert the removal. Do not delete or weaken the four rotation tests.
